title: Simple Interest

blocks.html: When you put money in a savings account, the bank pays you for using it. That payment is interest. With simple interest, each year you earn the same percent of the amount you put in.
$$I = Prt$$ $I$ is the interest, $P$ the principal (the money you start with), $r$ the yearly rate as a decimal, and $t$ the time in years. The balance at the end is $P + I$.

One year of interest is $r$ times the principal: $P \times r$. Simple interest pays that same amount every year, so after $t$ years you have $t$ of them: $(P \times r) \times t$. (Many real accounts pay "compound" interest, which also earns interest on old interest. You will meet that later.)

blocks.title: Interest and balance
blocks.q: You deposit \$800 at 3% simple interest per year. How much interest do you earn in 4 years, and what is the balance?

blocks.title: Time in months
blocks.q: \$1,200 earns 2.5% simple interest per year. How much interest after 6 months?
steps: Time must be in years: 6 months is $\frac{6}{12} = 0.5$ year.

blocks.title: Finding the rate
blocks.q: A \$2,000 deposit earns \$150 of simple interest in 3 years. What is the rate?

blocks.html: Two slips to watch: using $3$ instead of $0.03$ for 3% (the interest comes out 100 times too big), and using months as if they were years. Check: does the interest look like a small part of the principal?
